body.p: This Amendment is in response to the Final Office Action, dated April 24, 2024 ("Office Action"). Claims 1-26 are pending, claims 22-26 having been withdrawn, and claims 1-3, and 19- 21 having been amended. No new matter is added. Examination of the claims in view of the ensuing remarks is respectfully requested.

With regard to the drawings, the Examiner states that Figure 1 should be designated by a legend such as -Prior Art--. A corrected drawing sheet for Figure 1 designated by "PRIOR ART" and labeled "Replacement Sheet" is submitted herewith. Withdrawal of the objections is respectfully requested.

Examiner rejects claims 1-2, 5, 11-14, and 16-17 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dennis et al. (Dennis, US 2017/0074857) in view of Gupta et al. (US 2018/0271404) for reasons of record. Examiner rejects claims 6-8 as allegedly being unpatentable over Dennis in view of Gupta, and further in view of Saatchi et al. (Saatchi, US 2013/0165810) for reasons of record. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.

While Applicant does not concede to the merits of the rejections, in an effort to advance prosecution of the present application, independent claim 1 has been amended. Claim 1, as currently amended, recites:
"A system configured to determine concentrations of various gases using
multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient, the system comprising:
the multiple gas sensors, each gas sensor configured to output sensor data
relating to a concentration of a different gas passing through the gas flow path, wherein the multiple gas sensors comprise a CH4 sensor, a C02 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an
H2S sensor;
a control system comprising one or more processors and a memory for
determining concentrations of gases based on the output sensor data, the output sensor
Page 7 of 11
data comprising data output from the CH4 sensor, the CO2 sensor, the H2 sensor, and
the H2S sensor..."

According to amended claim 1, the claimed system has multiple gas sensors comprising a CH4 sensor, a CO2 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor, each gas sensor output sensor data relating to a concentration of a respective gas, i.e., CH4, CO2, H2, or H2S, passing through a gas flow path of a manifold. As described throughout the specification as originally filed, such a structure and arrangement of the multiple gas sensors allow testing all four gases at once in the same device/system to get accurate and consistent readings. For example, see paragraphs [0057]. That is, as described in paragraph [00101] of the specification, systems and methods have been developed to determine concentrations of multiple breath gases using multiple sensors with a single device and one breath sample from a patient because a reliable determination of whether a patient has SIBO may require testing each of C02, H2, H2S, and CH4 gases. Further, measuring each of these gasses with a single exhaled breath from a patient would be the most efficient and accurate way to determine these concentrations and apply a diagnostic algorithm. However, developing a system that can test multiple gases using multiple sensors is challenging for a variety of reasons, as described in paragraph [00102] of the specification. The claimed invention according to amended claims solves the problem in prior art.

Since features previously recited in claim 2 are now somewhat similarly recited (although "or" in previous claim 2 has been changed to "and" in current claim 1) in amended claim 1, the rejection of claim 2 is discussed here to support allowability of amended claim 1. With regard to the rejection of claim 2, the Examiner asserts that Dennis teaches "the at least one gas sensor further comprises at least one of a CO2 sensor (see entire document, especially [0024]-[0026], [0241], [0358], CO2 is sensed." (Emphasis added.) The Examiner further asserts that "Gupta teaches an H2 sensor, or an H2S sensor (see entire document, especially [0005], [0057])." (Emphasis added.) Paragraph [0005] of Gupta discloses that "[c]oncentrations of H2S, CH4 and H2 exhaled in the breath have been shown in numerous clinical studies to be linked to SIBO," and paragraph [0057] of Gupta discloses that "handheld analysis device may be utilized that can detect CO2, H2, and H2S using durable and reusable sensors" and that each of CO2, H2, and H2S could be detected with a different sensor.

Even if the asserted teachings by Dennis and Gupta are combined, they fail to disclose or teach, at least, a "system configured to determine concentrations of various gases using multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient," "the multiple gas sensors comprise a CH4 sensor, a CO2 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor," and "the output sensor data comprising data output from the CH4 sensor, the CO2 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor," as recited in amended claim 1. Saatchi fails to cure the above-identified deficiencies of Dennis and Gupta with respect to amended claim 1.

Accordingly, amended claim 1 and its dependent claims are allowable over the cited references. In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections.

Examiner rejects claims 1-4, 9-10, and 15 as allegedly being unpatentable over Pierry et al. (Pierry, US 20040186391) in view of Gupta for reasons of record. Applicant respectfully traverses this rejection.

With regard to the rejection of claim 1, the Examiner admits that Pierry does not teach that "the at least one gas sensor comprises a CH4 sensor." The Examiner cites paragraphs [0005] and [0057] of Gupta to cure the admitted deficiency of Pierry. Further, with regard to the rejection of claim 2, the Examiner asserts that "Pierry teaches sensors including at least CO2 and other gases" in paragraph [0041], and "Gupta teaches an H2 sensor and H2S sensor" in paragraphs [0005] and [0057]. (Emphasis added.) Paragraphs [0005] and [0057] of Gupta were discussed above with regard to the rejection of claim 1 by Dennis and Gupta.

Even if the asserted teachings by Pierry and Gupta are combined, they fail to disclose or teach, at least, a "system configured to determine concentrations of various gases using multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient," "the multiple gas sensors comprise a CH4 sensor, a CO2 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor," and "the output sensor data comprising data output from the CH4 sensor, the CO2 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor," as recited in amended claim 1.

Accordingly, amended claim 1 and its dependent claims are allowable over the cited references. In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections.

Examiner rejects claims 1-2, 18-19, and 21 as allegedly being unpatentable over Gupta in view of Dennis for reasons of record. Examiner rejects claim 20 as allegedly being unpatentable over Gupta in view of Dennis, and further in view of Pimentel et al. (Pimentel, WO 2018/156937 Al) for reasons of record. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections.

With regard to the rejection of claim 1, the Examiner asserts that Gupta teaches that "at least one gas sensor comprises a CH4 sensor." (Emphasis added.) Further, with regard to the rejection of claim 2, the Examiner asserts that "Gupta teaches wherein the at least one gas sensor further comprises at least one of a C02 sensor, an H2 sensor, or an H2S sensor" in paragraph [0059]. (Emphasis added.) Paragraph [0059] of Gupta discloses "a clinical medical device capable of detecting C02, H2, CH4, and H2S." (Emphasis added.)

Even if the asserted teachings by Gupta and Dennis are combined, they fail to disclose or teach, at least, a "system configured to determine concentrations of various gases using multiple gas sensors with one breath sample from a patient," "the multiple gas sensors comprise a CH4 sensor, a C02 sensor, an H2 sensor, and an H2S sensor," and "the output sensor data comprising data output from the CH4 sensor, the C02 sensor, the H2 sensor, and the H2S sensor," as recited in amended claim 1. Pimental fails to cure the above-identified deficiencies of Gupta and Dennis with respect to amended claim 1.

Accordingly, amended claim 1 and its dependent claims are allowable over the cited references. In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections.

All of the claims in the application are now believed to be allowable. Favorable consideration and a Notice of Allowance are earnestly solicited. If questions remain regarding this application, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at (213) 629-6000.
